jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Multimodal Foundation Models
jobs.description:
### **About Mecka AI**

Mecka AI is building the data infrastructure layer for robotics and embodied AI.  
We design and operate global systems for data capture, data labeling, and hardware-enabled workflows used by leading AI labs and robotics companies to train and validate humanoid and embodied AI systems.  
We work closely with frontier robotics teams to bridge real-world data, simulation, learning-based systems, and deployed hardware.

### **The role**

Every capture tells a story: what someone did, when they did it and whether they completed the task. At Mecka, you’ll build vision-language and video models that turn that footage into useful annotations and catch quality issues across more video than a human team could review.

You’ll own the work from data selection and training through evaluation and production. We’re looking for someone who brings strong research instincts and the engineering skills to make models reliable at scale—and who wants to understand where they fail as much as where they succeed.

### **What you’ll do**

* **Build models that understand the footage.** You’ll develop and improve vision-language and video models for egocentric and manipulation footage.
* **Catch problems across what we collect.** You’ll build model pipelines that identify capture defects, missing coverage and task errors, then check their performance against human audits.
* **Make models more reliable.** You’ll use supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization and reinforcement learning to improve reliability and reasoning.
* **Turn video into useful annotations.** You’ll build pipelines for captioning, temporal grounding and video annotation at scale.
* **Take experiments through to production.** You’ll run large experiments on distributed GPU infrastructure, analyze the results and turn successful approaches into production systems.

### **What you’ll bring**

* **Hands-on experience with large multimodal models.** You’ve trained, fine-tuned or post-trained vision-language or multimodal models.
* **Strong deep learning fundamentals.** You’re comfortable building and training models with PyTorch or JAX.
* **Experience running large experiments.** You can design an experiment, see it through and draw sound conclusions from the results.
* **Familiarity with distributed training.** You know your way around GPU-based development and distributed training infrastructure.
* **Research instincts and engineering discipline.** You ask good questions, test your assumptions and build clean systems that hold up beyond the experiment.

### **Nice to have**

Experience in one or more of these areas would be valuable:

* **Footage quality control:** Using vision-language and video models to identify defects and gaps in captured data.
* **Video understanding and annotation:** Structured captioning, temporal grounding and scene understanding.
* **Training and post-training:** Reward modeling, synthetic data, and data curation and filtering for multimodal models.

If you don't check every box above but believe you can do the job, we encourage you to apply — we're looking for capability and trajectory, not a perfect checklist match.

We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, we will partner with you to meet your needs.

We may use AI-assisted tools to help evaluate applications against the requirements of this role. These tools support our recruiting team in identifying qualified candidates but do not replace human judgment or limit which applications may be reviewed or considered.

Compensation Range: CA$140K - CA$200K

jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

The Creative X team within Amazon Advertising builds AI systems that understand and evaluate ad images and videos, so advertisers of every size can deliver high-quality experiences to customers. In this role, you will build image and video models that recognize what a creative contains, check whether it meets quality and brand requirements, and measure its effectiveness with measurable precision and recall.  
  
We invest in computer vision, video understanding, vision-language models (VLMs), multimodal representation learning, and evaluation science, including calibrating automated judges against human judgment. A central challenge is making these models work at scale: you will use techniques such as model distillation so that image and video understanding can run across billions of ad impressions. You will join a team of applied scientists, product managers and software developers, own science components from prototype to production, ship advertiser-facing features, and contribute to publications.  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* Build and improve image and video understanding models that extract semantic metadata from ad creatives, such as objects, products, scenes, text overlays, logos and brand elements, and shot-level events in video.
* Develop models and metrics that detect visual production defects (for example distorted products, garbled text, and temporal artifacts in video) and check whether creatives follow the brief, with measurable precision and recall.
* Apply methods through methods like distillation (and other techniques) to make efficient image and video understanding models, that are ready for production and can run at the scale of billions of daily ad impressions.
* Calibrate automated image and video judges against human annotations, using preference learning and active learning to raise agreement with expert reviewers.
* Run experiments, analyze the results, and turn findings into production improvements together with engineering and product partners. Share results in design reviews, documents and research publications.

  
About the team  
The Creative X team within Amazon Advertising is on a mission to democratize access to high-quality ad creatives for advertisers worldwide. We build the AI systems that determine what a creative contains; whether and why it will resonate with customers, working across images, video, audio, and text at Amazon-scale volume; and then serve the most performative ads to customers based on their personas. **About Ramp**
==============

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them.

A few things that define how we operate:

* **One team, one company, one objective.** There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle.
* **If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it.** We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack.
* **We go first, and we go fast.** When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed.
* **We lead the way.** We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job.
* **We stay calibrated.** Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.

**You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure.**

**Our Teams**
-------------

Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.

Right now, we operate across five areas:

* **Compute** — the foundation for running Ramp’s services and financial workflows: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and asynchronous execution and messaging systems, including Temporal. The team owns production runtime reliability, scaling, isolation, and safe rollouts.
* **Storage** — the production data foundations that underpin Ramp: databases, caching, and object storage, with ownership of reliability, performance, capacity, recovery, and safe data movement.
* **Developer Infrastructure** — the shared infrastructure that helps engineers ship and understand production: CI/CD systems, observability foundations for logs, metrics, and traces, and visibility into infrastructure usage and cost.
* **Compliance Platform** — the infrastructure and operational capabilities for Ramp’s government environments and compliance needs: secure access, deployment paths, environment validation, and technical controls that let product teams deliver reliably within regulatory and compliance requirements.
* **Reliability Platform** — the tools and operating model for understanding and improving customer-facing reliability and performance: SLA/SLO measurement and reporting, customer-health visibility, monitoring and paging, and incident response and follow-through. The team helps product teams remain accountable for the health of what they build.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

As a FinOps Specialist within Production Engineering, you’ll help Ramp make better decisions about infrastructure spend – from resource usage and cloud commitments to vendor contracts and new investments.

You’ll work closely with Production Engineering leadership, Developer Infrastructure, Finance, Procurement, and engineering teams across Ramp. You’ll bring financial depth, investigate opportunities independently, and partner with engineers to turn recommendations into measurable results.

This is a senior individual contributor role.

Day to day, you will:

* **Set direction for infrastructure cost management.** Identify the highest-impact opportunities across Ramp, establish priorities with Production Engineering leadership and partner teams, and build a roadmap that balances immediate savings with lasting improvements.
* **Understand and explain our spend.** Investigate costs across AWS, observability, and AI providers. Connect changes to usage, architecture, customer growth, and engineering decisions, and help teams distinguish expected investment from avoidable waste.

* **We stay calibrated.** Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.

**You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure.**

**Our Teams**
-------------

Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.

Right now, we operate across five areas:

* **Compute** — the foundation for running Ramp’s services and financial workflows: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and asynchronous execution and messaging systems, including Temporal. The team owns production runtime reliability, scaling, isolation, and safe rollouts.
* **Storage** — the production data foundations that underpin Ramp: databases, caching, and object storage, with ownership of reliability, performance, capacity, recovery, and safe data movement.
* **Developer Infrastructure** — the shared infrastructure that helps engineers ship and understand production: CI/CD systems, observability foundations for logs, metrics, and traces, and visibility into infrastructure usage and cost.
* **Compliance Platform** — the infrastructure and operational capabilities for Ramp’s government environments and compliance needs: secure access, deployment paths, environment validation, and technical controls that let product teams deliver reliably within regulatory and compliance requirements.
* **Reliability Platform** — the tools and operating model for understanding and improving customer-facing reliability and performance: SLA/SLO measurement and reporting, customer-health visibility, monitoring and paging, and incident response and follow-through. The team helps product teams remain accountable for the health of what they build.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

As a FinOps Specialist within Production Engineering, you’ll help Ramp make better decisions about infrastructure spend – from resource usage and cloud commitments to vendor contracts and new investments.

You’ll work closely with Production Engineering leadership, Developer Infrastructure, Finance, Procurement, and engineering teams across Ramp. You’ll bring financial depth, investigate opportunities independently, and partner with engineers to turn recommendations into measurable results.

This is a senior individual contributor role.

Day to day, you will:

* **Set direction for infrastructure cost management.** Identify the highest-impact opportunities across Ramp, establish priorities with Production Engineering leadership and partner teams, and build a roadmap that balances immediate savings with lasting improvements.
* **Understand and explain our spend.** Investigate costs across AWS, observability, and AI providers. Connect changes to usage, architecture, customer growth, and engineering decisions, and help teams distinguish expected investment from avoidable waste.
* **Embed with teams early.** Partner with product and infrastructure teams during design and planning. Help them evaluate cost implications, model how systems will scale, and make informed tradeoffs before committing to an architecture or vendor.
* **Build forecasts we can defend.** Work with engineers to understand upcoming launches, migrations, and capacity needs. Translate those plans into financial models that explain expected spend, key assumptions, and uncertainty.
* **Shape commitment and vendor strategy.** Model cloud discounts, commitment levels, pay

jobs.description:
### **About Mecka AI**

Mecka AI is building the data infrastructure layer for robotics and embodied AI.  
We design and operate global systems for data capture, data labeling, and hardware-enabled workflows used by leading AI labs and robotics companies to train and validate humanoid and embodied AI systems.  
We work closely with frontier robotics teams to bridge real-world data, simulation, learning-based systems, and deployed hardware.

### **The role**

When a robotics team trains on Mecka’s data, they need to trust what they’re getting. You’ll define what that trust rests on: the benchmarks, audits and quality standards behind every delivery. You’ll dig into the failures that averages hide, question results that look too good and make the call on whether data is ready to ship.

You’ll work across Computer Vision, annotation, operations and delivery. We’re looking for someone with a machine learning and data science background who enjoys getting to the bottom of a difficult measurement problem, and can turn what they find into a quality bar the whole team can use.

### **What you’ll do**

* Own the benchmark methodology: which evaluation sets exist, how they are sampled, which metrics apply and how versions are frozen and compared.
* Write customer quality specifications and audit rubrics, and keep both aligned with what customers actually reject.
* Run human audits and work with annotation and operations on sampling, agreement, throughput and cost.
* Build automated checks and graders that reduce manual review costs and are hard to game.
* Track where recorded hours are lost, report quality results regularly and make the ship or no-ship call on data.

### **What you need**

* Experience in evaluation, measurement or data quality for machine learning systems, or in data operations at scale.
* A machine learning and data science background, with strong Python and working knowledge of statistics: sampling, precision and recall, agreement and confidence intervals.
* Experience designing evaluation protocols and ground-truth pipelines from scratch.
* The judgment to challenge a research team’s numbers and support that challenge with evidence.
* An eye for how a metric can be gamed, and the habit of closing those gaps.

### **Nice to have**

* **Benchmarks and metrics:** 3D pose, trajectory and reconstruction metrics such as MPJPE and ATE.
* **Audits and data quality:** Sampling design, inter-annotator agreement, loss accounting and managing annotators or vendors.
* **Automated checks and graders:** Verifiers, learned scoring, active learning and human-in-the-loop evaluation.
* **Data curation and scoring:** Quality scoring, filtering and composition of large datasets.

If you don't check every box above but believe you can do the job, we encourage you to apply — we're looking for capability and trajectory, not a perfect checklist match.

We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, we will partner with you to meet your needs.

We may use AI-assisted tools to help evaluate applications against the requirements of this role. These tools support our recruiting team in identifying qualified candidates but do not replace human judgment or limit which applications may be reviewed or considered.

Compensation Range: CA$140K - CA$200K

new_jobs.description:
### **About Mecka AI**

Mecka AI is building the data infrastructure layer for robotics and embodied AI.  
We design and operate global systems for data capture, data labeling, and hardware-enabled workflows used by leading AI labs and robotics companies to train and validate humanoid and embodied AI systems.  
We work closely with frontier robotics teams to bridge real-world data, simulation, learning-based systems, and deployed hardware.

### **The role**

Mecka captures how people move, work and interact with the physical world. The footage is messy: hands disappear behind objects, cameras turn quickly, and motion blur hides the details. You’ll build models that make sense of it—and turn it into accurate 3D data that robotics teams can train on.

We’re looking for machine learning engineers with depth in pose estimation, SLAM or 3D reconstruction who want to own what happens after the experiment works. You’ll train models, investigate where they fail and get them running reliably in production, working across the perception stack along the way.

### **What you’ll do**

* **Build models for the problems in front of us.** You’ll train vision models from scratch on large multi-view, multi-sensor datasets, developing new losses and architectures where existing methods fall short.
* **Work through the difficult footage.** You’ll tackle motion blur, fast rotation, heavy occlusion and partial views of hands, bodies and objects.
* **Find out where your models fail.** You’ll evaluate them on our own video, measuring real error and failure rates alongside public benchmark results.
* **Own the path to production.** You’ll optimize GPU performance, make results reproducible, integrate models into our data pipeline and ship releases you can roll back.
* **Follow problems through to a fix.** You’ll reproduce customer-reported issues, understand what went wrong and deliver a fix. You’ll also prototype quickly as new perception problems come up.

### **What you’ll bring**

* **Strong machine learning fundamentals.** You’re comfortable building and training models with Python and PyTorch.
* **Experience training large vision models from scratch.** Your experience goes beyond running or fine-tuning existing models.
* **Depth in a computer vision specialty.** You’ve worked deeply in at least one area, such as pose estimation, SLAM or 3D reconstruction.
* **Experience owning models in production.** You’ve shipped a model or perception component and stayed responsible for it afterward.
* **Comfort with the work as it is.** You can make progress with noisy real-world data and adapt when priorities shift.

### **Nice to have**

Experience in one or more of these areas would be valuable:

* **Hand and body tracking:** 3D hand and full-body tracking, mesh recovery, human-object and human-scene interaction, and estimating contact with objects and the ground.
* **SLAM, VIO and calibration:** Learned ego-motion, optical flow, online calibration and metric scale.
* **3D reconstruction and objects:** Feed-forward or per-scene reconstruction, Gaussian splatting or NeRF, and neural 3D object estimation from egocentric video.

This role combines strong software engineering fundamentals with hands-on data engineering. You’ll build ETL/ELT pipelines, design data models and contracts, strengthen data quality, and apply AI to meaningfully improve our workflows and products.

### **About Mecka AI**

Mecka AI is building the data infrastructure layer for robotics and embodied AI.  
We design and operate global systems for data capture, data labeling, and hardware-enabled workflows used by leading AI labs and robotics companies to train and validate humanoid and embodied AI systems.  
We work closely with frontier robotics teams to bridge real-world data, simulation, learning-based systems, and deployed hardware.

### **The role**

Every capture tells a story: what someone did, when they did it and whether they completed the task. At Mecka, you’ll build vision-language and video models that turn that footage into useful annotations and catch quality issues across more video than a human team could review.

You’ll own the work from data selection and training through evaluation and production. We’re looking for someone who brings strong research instincts and the engineering skills to make models reliable at scale—and who wants to understand where they fail as much as where they succeed.

### **What you’ll do**

* **Build models that understand the footage.** You’ll develop and improve vision-language and video models for egocentric and manipulation footage.
* **Catch problems across what we collect.** You’ll build model pipelines that identify capture defects, missing coverage and task errors, then check their performance against human audits.
* **Make models more reliable.** You’ll use supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization and reinforcement learning to improve reliability and reasoning.
* **Turn video into useful annotations.** You’ll build pipelines for captioning, temporal grounding and video annotation at scale.
* **Take experiments through to production.** You’ll run large experiments on distributed GPU infrastructure, analyze the results and turn successful approaches into production systems.

### **What you’ll bring**

* **Hands-on experience with large multimodal models.** You’ve trained, fine-tuned or post-trained vision-language or multimodal models.
* **Strong deep learning fundamentals.** You’re comfortable building and training models with PyTorch or JAX.
* **Experience running large experiments.** You can design an experiment, see it through and draw sound conclusions from the results.
* **Familiarity with distributed training.** You know your way around GPU-based development and distributed training infrastructure.
* **Research instincts and engineering discipline.** You ask good questions, test your assumptions and build clean systems that hold up beyond the experiment.

### **Nice to have**

Experience in one or more of these areas would be valuable:

* **Footage quality control:** Using vision-language and video models to identify defects and gaps in captured data.
* **Video understanding and annotation:** Structured captioning, temporal grounding and scene understanding.
* **Training and post-training:** Reward modeling, synthetic data, and data curation and filtering for multimodal models.

If you don't check every box above but believe you can do the job, we encourage you to apply — we're looking for capability and trajectory, not a perfect checklist match.

### **About the Team**

The Foundations Research team works on high-risk, high-reward ideas that could shape the next decade of AI. Our goal is to advance the science and data that enable our training and scaling efforts, with a particular focus on future frontier models. We push the boundaries of data, scaling laws, optimization techniques, model architectures, model + search co-design and efficiency improvements to propel our science.

The Search team sits within Foundationsation. In close partnership with researchers, we bring modeling advances into production and improve how AI systems discover, retrieve, and use knowledge.

### **About the Role**

We’re looking for a Researcher to lead our safety and alignment research: building the systems that distinguish useful web content from spam, manipulation, and other adversarial or low-quality material.

The challenge extends beyond evaluating individual pages. A page may appear credible in isolations, metadata, or relationships with other sites reveal coordinated manipulation. As AI makes convincing content easier to produce at scale, detection systems must adapt to increasingly sophisticated adversaries.

You’ll define the technical approach, build classifiers and evaluations, and shape how integrity signals influence what Search indexes and retrieves. Working closely with Search and broader Safety and Integrity teams, you’ll use frontier models to advance detection methods and bring them into production.

### **Responsibilities**

* Define the technical direction for Safety + Integrity, identifying gaps and determining which problems and interventions to prioritize.
* Develop AI and ML systems to detect spam, scams, phishing, malicious domains, prompt injections, and other adversarial or low-quality web content.
* Discover useful signals across page contents, domains, metadata, and relationships between websites, including patterns that reveal coordinated manipulation.
* Build evaluations that measure detection quality and how integrity interventions affect the information Search surfaces.
* Translate detection signals into indexing, ranking, and filtering decisions, improving what models can retrieve and rely on.
* Serve as the technical owner for integrity within Search, partnering with researchers, engineers, and broader Safety and Integrity teams to build and deploy these systems.

* Deep experience in web spam, search quality, adversarial content detection, or related integrity problems at scale.
* Strong applied ML and research skills, with experience developing classifiers, detection methods, and evaluations for real-world systems.

**About Lumafield:**

Lumafield was founded in 2019 to upgrade manufacturing.

We are engineers with deep experience across the product development cycle, from initial ideas to shipping hardware, across industries and specializations, who became frustrated by the cost and complexity of modern manufacturing. So we decided to upgrade it.

Engineers make million-dollar decisions every day, and they need tools that give them the greatest possible insight into their products. By offering unprecedented visibility into products, as well as AI-driven tools that highlight problems and generate quantitative data, Lumafield promises to revolutionize the way complex products are created, manufactured, and used across industries. We started with industrial CT scanning, which for us was the most valuable but underutilized tool in the manufacturing toolbox, enabling us to rapidly inspect essential components non-destructively.

We rebuilt the whole system, from X-ray capture, to computer vision analysis, to web-based collaboration, to the entire business model, making the most advanced manufacturing tech more accessible to every industry. Our company, like our platform, is designed for upgrades. We’re building for greater intelligence, autonomy, and speed. For deeper vision, operational excellence, and powerful insights. And then we'll upgrade it all again.

Lumafield is headquartered in San Francisco, CA. and has an office in Cambridge, MA.

**About the role:**

As a Cloud DevOps Engineer at Lumafield, you will own the cloud platform that runs Voyager, our CT data platform. A scan is only useful once someone can open it, measure it, and make a decision, and that happens in Voyager, in a web browser. Everything underneath is yours: AWS, the production Kubernetes clusters, Terraform, the pipeline every engineer ships through, observability, and the cloud side of our security and compliance programs.

This is an ownership role, not a ticket queue. Nobody will hand you a backlog; you will be the person who knows what the platform needs, what it costs, and what to fix first. We expect you to grow into a senior engineer here.

You will work in Platform Engineering alongside the backend lead, the software engineers who ship through your pipeline every day, and the team building the on-prem version of Voyager for customers who cannot send scan data to the cloud. You will report to engineering leadership; Platform Engineering is part of the organization our new Head of Software will lead.

This is a hands-on, in-person role based in our San Francisco, CA office.

* Own our AWS accounts and regions: architecture, access, onboarding and offboarding, and a bill you can explain by service and environment, then bring down
* Run the production EKS clusters, and carry Kubernetes version upgrades from plan and rehearsal to completion, with a rollback ready
* Keep infrastructure and Kubernetes configuration in Terraform, so changes go through code review instead of the console
* Own CI/CD - GitHub Actions, CI runners, artifact and image storage, and GitOps deploys with ArgoCD - and make it faster and more reliable in ways engineers notice
* Own observability (Sentry, Logz.io and Postman today) and decide what the platform needs next; take on-call, and close every incident with a written postmortem and a fix
* Own the cloud side of our SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 programs: least-privilege access, logging, encryption, cluster hardening, and audit evidence that comes out of the system instead of being assembled by hand
* Partner with our IT team on shared controls, and raise the platform's security bar as we maintain CMMC Level 1 and ITAR compliance and work toward FedRAMP 20x
* Document the platform - runbooks, postmortems, and design notes - so it does not live in one person's head

### **About you:**

* You have been on the hook for a production platform: releases, incidents, and on-call
* You have upgraded a production Kubernetes cluster and can tell us what went wrong and what you changed afterwards
* You write Terraform that other people depend on, and you are comfortable with modules, state, and reading a plan before you apply it
* You have built or rebuilt a CI/CD pipeline that engineers used daily
* You have opened a cloud bill, found what was driving it, and changed it
* You have implemented a security control or produced audit evidence for a program such as SOC 2 or ISO 27001, or done the equivalent access and hardening work without the audit

Overview:

**ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD.**

At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future.

Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career.

Responsibilities:

**THE ROLE:**

Join AMD IT’s Compute Platforms Engineering team and help build the infrastructure powering high-performance computing, distributed AI training, and inference workloads. As an HPC & AI Infrastructure Engineer, you will work in a highly technical, hands-on environment supporting large-scale CPU and GPU compute platforms across on-premises and cloud environments.

This is an opportunity to work at the intersection of AI, HPC, GPU computing, high-speed networking, storage, and cloud infrastructure. You will help bring new compute capabilities into production, improve the performance and reliability of existing platforms, and gain exposure to evolving technologies supporting increasingly complex AI and engineering workloads. You will collaborate with infrastructure architects, network and operations engineers, researchers, cloud providers, and hardware and technology partners to solve challenging systems problems and deliver scalable computing solutions.

**THE PERSON:**

You are a collaborative and curious engineer who enjoys solving complex infrastructure problems and understanding how systems perform from end to end. You approach troubleshooting methodically, use data to guide decisions, and look for opportunities to improve reliability and simplify operations through automation. You communicate technical information clearly, work effectively with globally distributed teams, and are comfortable independently delivering defined engineering work while collaborating with technical experts on broader architectural decisions.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Deploy, configure, and maintain Linux-based CPU and GPU compute clusters supporting HPC, distributed AI training, and inference workloads.
* Administer and optimize workload environments utilizing technologies such as Slurm and Kubernetes, including scheduling, resource allocation, access, and workload troubleshooting.
* Support AI and distributed computing platforms by managing software environments, containers, GPU runtimes, and workload deployments.
* Automate infrastructure provisioning, configuration, and lifecycle management using scripting, configuration management, and infrastructure-as-code practices.
* Validate compute hardware, BIOS, firmware, GPU drivers, and software compatibility and support platform upgrades through testing, rollout, and rollback planning.
* Configure and troubleshoot host networking for HPC and GPU environments, including high-speed NICs, RDMA interfaces, VLANs, MTU configuration, IP addressing, and routing.
* Partner with network engineering teams to deploy and validate high-performance RoCEv2 or InfiniBand fabrics and investigate connectivity, congestion, and end-to-end RDMA performance.
* Troubleshoot complex issues spanning compute, GPU, networking, storage, virtualization, container, and cloud environments.
* Perform cluster acceptance testing and workload benchmarking to identify performance bottlenecks and improve system performance, utilization, scalability, and reliability.
* Develop and enhance monitoring, dashboards, and alerting while contributing to incident resolution, root-cause analysis, and preventive improvements.
* Partner with security and operations teams to maintain platform security, apply updates, and address vulnerabilities.
* Develop and maintain technical documentation, operating procedures, deployment guidance, and troubleshooting runbooks.
* Collaborate with internal infrastructure teams, cloud providers, and technology and hardware partners to introduce new compute capabilities and resolve complex technical challenges.

**PREFERRED EXPERIENCE:**

* Hands-on experience with Linux systems engineering, HPC infrastructure, distributed computing, GPU infrastructure, or large-scale compute environments.
* Experience deploying, administering, or supporting production of HPC or GPU compute clusters.
* Strong Linux administration and troubleshooting skills across operating systems, networking, storage, and system performance.
* Experience with Slurm, Kubernetes, or comparable workload scheduling and orchestration platforms.

new_jobs.description:
### **About Mecka AI**

Mecka AI is building the data infrastructure layer for robotics and embodied AI.  
We design and operate global systems for data capture, data labeling, and hardware-enabled workflows used by leading AI labs and robotics companies to train and validate humanoid and embodied AI systems.  
We work closely with frontier robotics teams to bridge real-world data, simulation, learning-based systems, and deployed hardware.

### **The role**

When a robotics team trains on Mecka’s data, they need to trust what they’re getting. You’ll define what that trust rests on: the benchmarks, audits and quality standards behind every delivery. You’ll dig into the failures that averages hide, question results that look too good and make the call on whether data is ready to ship.

You’ll work across Computer Vision, annotation, operations and delivery. We’re looking for someone with a machine learning and data science background who enjoys getting to the bottom of a difficult measurement problem, and can turn what they find into a quality bar the whole team can use.

### **What you’ll do**

* Own the benchmark methodology: which evaluation sets exist, how they are sampled, which metrics apply and how versions are frozen and compared.
* Write customer quality specifications and audit rubrics, and keep both aligned with what customers actually reject.
* Run human audits and work with annotation and operations on sampling, agreement, throughput and cost.
* Build automated checks and graders that reduce manual review costs and are hard to game.
* Track where recorded hours are lost, report quality results regularly and make the ship or no-ship call on data.

### **What you need**

* Experience in evaluation, measurement or data quality for machine learning systems, or in data operations at scale.
* A machine learning and data science background, with strong Python and working knowledge of statistics: sampling, precision and recall, agreement and confidence intervals.
* Experience designing evaluation protocols and ground-truth pipelines from scratch.
* The judgment to challenge a research team’s numbers and support that challenge with evidence.
* An eye for how a metric can be gamed, and the habit of closing those gaps.

### **Nice to have**

* **Benchmarks and metrics:** 3D pose, trajectory and reconstruction metrics such as MPJPE and ATE.
* **Audits and data quality:** Sampling design, inter-annotator agreement, loss accounting and managing annotators or vendors.
* **Automated checks and graders:** Verifiers, learned scoring, active learning and human-in-the-loop evaluation.
* **Data curation and scoring:** Quality scoring, filtering and composition of large datasets.

If you don't check every box above but believe you can do the job, we encourage you to apply — we're looking for capability and trajectory, not a perfect checklist match.

Mecka AI is building the data infrastructure layer for robotics and embodied AI.

### **The role**

Mecka captures how people move, work and interact with the physical world. The footage is messy: hands disappear behind objects, cameras turn quickly, and motion blur hides the details. You’ll build models that make sense of it—and turn it into accurate 3D data that robotics teams can train on.

We’re looking for machine learning engineers with depth in pose estimation, SLAM or 3D reconstruction who want to own what happens after the experiment works. You’ll train models, investigate where they fail and get them running reliably in production, working across the perception stack along the way.

### **What you’ll do**

* **Build models for the problems in front of us.** You’ll train vision models from scratch on large multi-view, multi-sensor datasets, developing new losses and architectures where existing methods fall short.
* **Work through the difficult footage.** You’ll tackle motion blur, fast rotation, heavy occlusion and partial views of hands, bodies and objects.
* **Find out where your models fail.** You’ll evaluate them on our own video, measuring real error and failure rates alongside public benchmark results.
* **Own the path to production.** You’ll optimize GPU performance, make results reproducible, integrate models into our data pipeline and ship releases you can roll back.
* **Follow problems through to a fix.** You’ll reproduce customer-reported issues, understand what went wrong and deliver a fix. You’ll also prototype quickly as new perception problems come up.

### **What you’ll bring**

* **Strong machine learning fundamentals.** You’re comfortable building and training models with Python and PyTorch.
* **Experience training large vision models from scratch.** Your experience goes beyond running or fine-tuning existing models.
* **Depth in a computer vision specialty.** You’ve worked deeply in at least one area, such as pose estimation, SLAM or 3D reconstruction.
* **Experience owning models in production.** You’ve shipped a model or perception component and stayed responsible for it afterward.
* **Comfort with the work as it is.** You can make progress with noisy real-world data and adapt when priorities shift.

Substack’s model, based on direct subscriptions, has fueled an explosion of independent publishing. It empowers creators with economic autonomy, creative ownership, and a direct connection to their most engaged audiences.

As a Software Engineer at Substack, you are responsible for the core product platform, from APIs, low-level services, and database operations, to frontend UI and testing. On the Video team you’ll be working on podcasting, live streaming, video and audio recording, uploading, clipping, and everything related to an excellent video product experience. Full Stack Engineers work in close partnership with designers, product thinkers, and customers directly to build out new product offerings and tooling across the platform. They are on the front-lines of product development and are responsible for creating what’s next for Substack.

**Responsibilities**

* With the support of the engineering team, develop the core Substack product for creators and consumers. This is a dynamic organization with needs across the board. We expect that engineers will be able to jump into any area of the product, learn quickly and add value.
* Support and collaborate with other team members, including engineers, designers, creators, support staff, and many others.
* Own your work and deliver high-quality solutions from product concept and proposal to implementation, experimentation, and measurement.
* Work directly with customers to solve their problems. The entire company (CEO included) participates in customer support in order to drive empathy for our users and help us build better products.
* We work with TypeScript, especially Node/Express and React, and Postgres. It’s helpful if you know these technologies already, if not, we’ll be excited to help you learn.
* We work to stay on the leading edge of AI tooling, to both improve our internal workflows, as well as utilize them in product to improve publisher capabilities and experiences

**Requirements**

* 4+ years of non-internship professional full stack web software development.
* Proficiency with Node.js and React is an advantage.
* Have a degree in Computer Science or have the equivalent industry experience.
* Independent and autonomous. We’re too small to micromanage, and expect that every person at the company owns their work and can be a leader.
* Take pride in building elegant and delightful product experiences. Substack works best when it gets out of the way so creators can focus on creating and connecting with their readers.
* Enjoy collaboration with a diverse group of thinkers while bringing our own unique experience and background to the team.
* Believe in Substack’s mission to build a better business model for content creation.
* Proficiency with video processing frameworks and libraries such as FFmpeg is an advantage.
* Experience with workflow systems such as Temporal is an advantage.

Substack’s compensation package includes a market competitive salary, equity for all full time roles, and exceptional benefits. Our cash compensation salary range for this role is $140,000 - $260,000. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate experience and expertise and may vary from the amounts listed above.

Substack is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or transgender status), age, national origin, veteran or disability status. We’re seeking people passionate about enabling independent expression and building a better business model for creators. If you want to see what media, communities, and content can become when unmoored from advertising models, and you have the skills and experience to contribute, we’d love to meet you.

Please see our Privacy Notice for details regarding Substack's collection and use of personal information relating to the application and recruitment process by clicking here.

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them.

A few things that define how we operate:

* **If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it.** We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack.
* **We go first, and we go fast.** When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed.
* **We lead the way.** We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job.
* **We stay calibrated.** Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.

**You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure.**

-------------

Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.

Right now, we operate across five areas:

* **Storage** — the production data foundations that underpin Ramp: databases, caching, and object storage, with ownership of reliability, performance, capacity, recovery, and safe data movement.

* **Compliance Platform** — the infrastructure and operational capabilities for Ramp’s government environments and compliance needs: secure access, deployment paths, environment validation, and technical controls that let product teams deliver reliably within regulatory and compliance requirements.
* **Reliability Platform** — the tools and operating model for understanding and improving customer-facing reliability and performance: SLA/SLO measurement and reporting, customer-health visibility, monitoring and paging, and incident response and follow-through. You’ll work closely with Production Engineering leadership, Developer Infrastructure, Finance, Procurement, and engineering teams across Ramp. You’ll bring financial depth, investigate opportunities independently, and partner with engineers to turn recommendations into measurable results.

new_jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Evals & Data Quality
new_jobs.description:
### **About Mecka AI**

Mecka AI is building the data infrastructure layer for robotics and embodied AI.  
We design and operate global systems for data capture, data labeling, and hardware-enabled workflows used by leading AI labs and robotics companies to train and validate humanoid and embodied AI systems.  
We work closely with frontier robotics teams to bridge real-world data, simulation, learning-based systems, and deployed hardware.

### **The role**

When a robotics team trains on Mecka’s data, they need to trust what they’re getting. You’ll define what that trust rests on: the benchmarks, audits and quality standards behind every delivery. You’ll dig into the failures that averages hide, question results that look too good and make the call on whether data is ready to ship.

You’ll work across Computer Vision, annotation, operations and delivery. We’re looking for someone with a machine learning and data science background who enjoys getting to the bottom of a difficult measurement problem, and can turn what they find into a quality bar the whole team can use.

### **What you’ll do**

* Own the benchmark methodology: which evaluation sets exist, how they are sampled, which metrics apply and how versions are frozen and compared.
* Write customer quality specifications and audit rubrics, and keep both aligned with what customers actually reject.
* Run human audits and work with annotation and operations on sampling, agreement, throughput and cost.
* Build automated checks and graders that reduce manual review costs and are hard to game.
* Track where recorded hours are lost, report quality results regularly and make the ship or no-ship call on data.

### **What you need**

* Experience in evaluation, measurement or data quality for machine learning systems, or in data operations at scale.
* A machine learning and data science background, with strong Python and working knowledge of statistics: sampling, precision and recall, agreement and confidence intervals.
* Experience designing evaluation protocols and ground-truth pipelines from scratch.
* The judgment to challenge a research team’s numbers and support that challenge with evidence.
* An eye for how a metric can be gamed, and the habit of closing those gaps.

### **Nice to have**

* **Benchmarks and metrics:** 3D pose, trajectory and reconstruction metrics such as MPJPE and ATE.
* **Audits and data quality:** Sampling design, inter-annotator agreement, loss accounting and managing annotators or vendors.
* **Automated checks and graders:** Verifiers, learned scoring, active learning and human-in-the-loop evaluation.
* **Data curation and scoring:** Quality scoring, filtering and composition of large datasets.

If you don't check every box above but believe you can do the job, we encourage you to apply — we're looking for capability and trajectory, not a perfect checklist match.

We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, we will partner with you to meet your needs.

We may use AI-assisted tools to help evaluate applications against the requirements of this role. These tools support our recruiting team in identifying qualified candidates but do not replace human judgment or limit which applications may be reviewed or considered.

Compensation Range: CA$140K - CA$200K
